approach: Teach the respectful titles a newcomer meets (don, doña, and professional titles such as licenciado and ingeniero) with how each is used, then the courtesy phrase con permiso, and practice choosing the right form of address.
coverage: Don and doña show respect and go with the first name: don Manuel, doña Rosa
Don and doña are not used with the surname alone
Professional titles go with the surname: licenciada Ruiz, ingeniero Torres, doctora Pérez
Licenciado, licenciada: a university graduate; very common in Mexico and Central America, especially for lawyers
Ingeniero, ingeniera: an engineer; doctor, doctora: a physician or a PhD; arquitecto, arquitecta
Speaking to the person, no article: Buenos días, licenciada Ruiz. Speaking about them: la licenciada Ruiz
Con permiso = excuse me (to pass or to leave); disculpe = excuse me (to get attention)

blocks.purpose: Explains why titles matter in Spanish-speaking workplaces and neighborhoods.

paragraphs: In much of Latin America, using a title is how you show respect, especially at work and with older people. Getting it right makes a warm first impression; leaving it off can sound too casual.
There are two families of titles: don and doña, which go with a first name, and professional titles, which go with a surname.

blocks.purpose: Contrasts the two families of titles and what each one goes with.

blocks.purpose: Targets putting don with a surname, the most common title error.

data.question: Your elderly neighbor is Manuel Gómez. How do you greet him with respect?

trapReasons.1: Mr. goes with the surname in English, so don seems to as well.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Learners map don onto Mr., and Mr. takes a surname.
data.correctReasoning: Don and doña go with the first name: don Manuel. No article when you speak to him.
data.recoveryTip: Don and doña: first name. Professional titles: surname.

blocks.purpose: Applies the professional titles in a workplace greeting.

data.prompt: Your company's engineer is Laura Méndez. Which greeting fits at work?

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Read the feedback and try again.

byOption.a: Yes: the feminine title ingeniera with her surname.
byOption.b: Ingeniero is for a man; for a woman it is ingeniera.
byOption.c: Doña goes with a first name, and at work the professional title fits better.
byOption.d: Speaking to her, leave out la.

blocks.purpose: Closes with the rule of which title goes with which name.

data.takeaway: Don and doña go with the first name; licenciado, ingeniero, doctor and arquitecto go with the surname; say con permiso to pass and disculpe to get attention.

checks.prompt: You need to walk between two people who are talking. What do you say?
checks.rationale: Con permiso asks to be let through or to leave; mucho gusto is nice to meet you and buenas tardes is a greeting.
checks.hint: You are asking permission to pass.

checks.prompt: Which greeting is correct for a woman named Rosa Fernández, the respected owner of the corner store?
checks.rationale: Doña is the feminine title and it goes with the first name, with no article when speaking to her.
